source.citation: Thompson, D'Arcy W. (1917) On Growth and Form. Cambridge University Press. Chapter XIII 'The Shapes of Horns, and of Teeth or Tusks: with a Note on Torsion', pp. 612-634, Figs. 318-324.
source.helico_spiral_formula_pages: Ch. XI, pp. 518 and 558-559 (R = e^(2 pi sin(beta) cot(alpha)) and the table of alpha vs beta)

claim_text: Horns (ram, goat, Ovis ammon) are logarithmic spirals wound on a cone (a conical helicoid generated by gnomonic growth), differing between species by the spiral constants and torsion.

published_model.name: Conical helico-spiral (logarithmic spiral wound on a cone) generated by gnomonic accretion at a basal growth zone
published_model.coordinate_system: Cylindrical (rho, theta, z) about the axis of the enveloping cone; theta increases from the horn tip (oldest part, smallest rho) towards the basal growth zone (youngest part, largest rho).

equations.name: Plane logarithmic (equiangular) spiral
equations.formula: rho(theta) = a * exp(k * theta),   k = cot(alpha)
equations.variables: rho: distance from the pole; theta: polar angle; a: scale (rho at theta = 0); alpha: constant spiral angle between radius vector and tangent
equations.thompson_locus: Ch. XI (equation of the logarithmic spiral), applied to horns on pp. 612-617

equations.name: Logarithmic spiral wound on a cone (helico-spiral)
equations.formula: rho(theta) = a * exp(theta * sin(beta) * cot(alpha));  z(theta) = rho(theta) * cot(beta)
equations.variables: beta: semi-angle of the enveloping cone (beta = 90 deg gives the plane/discoid spiral); alpha: spiral angle measured on the developed cone surface
equations.thompson_locus: Ch. XI p. 518 and p. 558; Ch. XIII p. 617 ('the helicoid component of the spire ... the angle theta (here beta)')

equations.name: Whorl ratio (consecutive-whorl breadth ratio)
equations.formula: R = rho(theta + 2 pi) / rho(theta) = exp(2 pi sin(beta) cot(alpha))
equations.variables: R: ratio of radii one full turn apart
equations.thompson_locus: Ch. XI p. 558 'Our formula ... now becomes R = e^(2 pi sin theta cot alpha)'

equations.name: Gnomonic growth (self-similarity) of the generating curve
equations.formula: w(theta) = c * rho(theta)   (horn breadth across the whorl scales with the same exponent k as the edge radius; every increment is a gnomon to the whole)
equations.variables: w: breadth of the horn measured across the whorl; c: constant
equations.thompson_locus: Ch. XI pp. 508-515 (theory of gnomons); Ch. XIII p. 618 (tapering 'due to the growth in its own plane of the generating curve')

equations.name: Unequal basal growth velocities generate the spiral
equations.formula: v_outer / v_inner = const > 1  =>  logarithmic spiral; v_outer = v_inner => straight horn; max/min velocities not diametrically opposite => helical (space) spiral
equations.variables: v_outer, v_inner: net longitudinal growth velocities on opposite sides of the basal annulus
equations.thompson_locus: Ch. XIII pp. 616, 619-620 (summary of the argument)

equations.name: Trihedral edge-length ratio of Ovis ammon
equations.variables: arc lengths of the three edges of the trihedral horn prism

state_variables: z (axial coordinate along the cone axis)
published_model.boundary_conditions: Horn tip at theta = 0 (rho = a); growth zone at the base at theta = theta_max; the horn is a finite arc of the spiral (typically 0.5 - 1.3 whorls in sheep and goats).

parameter_regime_table.alpha_deg: very small spiral angle in Thompson's words = nearly straight horn (interpreted as alpha -> 0 cot-convention: horn nearly straight)
parameter_regime_table.thompson_text: p. 616 'the spiral angle is very small, or in other words the horn is very nearly straight'
p. 617 'a beautiful logarithmic spiral, with a constant angle of rather less than 70 deg'

parameter_regime_table.taxon: Argali group (O. poli vs O. ammon / O. hodgsoni)
parameter_regime_table.beta: differs greatly: O. poli long-drawn-out (acute cone, small beta), O. ammon 'wound round a much blunter cone' (large beta)

note_on_alpha_convention: Thompson's 'spiral angle' alpha is the equiangular constant between radius vector and tangent (alpha = 90 deg is a circle; alpha -> 0 is a straight ray). His 'very small' for Oryx is used loosely for nearly straight horns, but his numbers for sheep/goats (70-75 deg) are the equiangular constant with cot(alpha) = k = d ln(rho)/d theta.

empirical_claims.claim: In the great majority of horns a continuous logarithmic spiral is recognisable (rhinoceros, sheep, goats, most antelopes).
Ovis ammon spiral angle about 75 deg; Highland ram a little more; wild goats < 70 deg; Oryx 20-40 deg.
empirical_claims.tested_here: partially (Ovis ammon and Capra sinaitica figures)

empirical_claims.claim: Species of Argali share nearly the same alpha but differ in the helical (cone) component beta.
empirical_claims.why: needs orthographic frontal+lateral pairs or 3D centrelines for several Argali species

empirical_claims.claim: Thicker horns are more spirally curved; slender horns are gently curved.
The sinuous ring boundaries are St Venant torsion warping of a twisted triangular prism.
Growth is gnomonic: tapering is produced by growth of the generating curve in its own plane, so the whole form is self-similar.
Musk ox and chamois horns are NOT logarithmic spirals (shape changes with age because the core bends/absorbs).

digitised_specimens.kind: Thompson's own 1917 lateral line drawing (Fig. 320, p. 621)
digitised_specimens.sector_note: Angles in the mathematical convention (x right, y up, degrees) about the pole guess; the sector runs clockwise from the basal growth zone (150 deg, top-left where the horn meets the frontal bone) through the top (90), the posterior extremity (0) and the ventral arc (-90) to where the ventral horn edge merges with the mandible outline (-125). The breadth sector is the part of the whorl where a ray from the pole crosses only horn (no skull). The mandible junction at the -125 deg end is trimmed automatically by the monotone-ln-rho rule (trim_non_monotone_ends).

digitised_specimens.species: Capra sinaitica (Nubian ibex) - Thompson's 'Arabian wild goat'
digitised_specimens.kind: Thompson's own 1917 lateral halftone (Fig. 319, p. 616, after Sclater P.Z.S.)
digitised_specimens.sector_note: Far (upper-left) horn only, because it is the outermost structure over its whole length: outer (dorsal) edge from the base above the ear (212 deg = -148 deg, lower-left) up the left side (168), over the crown (101) to the tip (61 deg). Sectors whose end exceeds 180 wrap through +/-180. About half a whorl, so alpha is weakly constrained; the fit is reported with a bootstrap CI. No breadth test (inner edge occluded by the near horn).

digitised_specimens.kind: Real specimen photograph (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0, Ksuryawanshi 2011, South Gobi, Mongolia)
digitised_specimens.sector_note: The bleached skull is low-saturation and is excluded by the HSV mask, so the mask is the horn sheath alone. Outer-edge sector runs clockwise from the base (140 deg, where the sheath meets the frontal) over the crown (90), the posterior extremity (0) and the ventral arc (-90) to where the tip passes behind the mandible (-118). Breadth sector [-100, 140] is where a ray from the pole crosses the hollow of the whorl (inner edge visible) and the sheath only. Not an orthographic axial view: perspective and the lateral flare of the tip are uncorrected (limitation recorded in README). Sensitivity sectors drop the ventral/tip arc, which visibly flares towards the camera (out of the spiral plane) and therefore violates the axial-projection assumption of E2.

registry_named_dataset.status: DATASET_MISMATCH_FOR_SHAPE - species match (Ovis, Capra), variables do not (horn length vs body mass only). Labelled analogue; not used for the verdict.

acceptance_criteria.a_log_spiral_form: log spiral beats the circle null by delta-AIC >= 10, is not beaten by the Archimedean spiral by more than 10, and Pearson |r|(ln rho, theta) >= 0.90 on every Ovis ammon source (primary sector; sensitivity sectors reported)
acceptance_criteria.b_alpha_thompson: alpha_proj is compared with Thompson's 75 deg through E2: consistent iff |alpha_proj - 75| <= 5 deg (plane spiral) OR k_proj <= cot(75 deg) so that a real cone semi-angle beta exists; alpha is not identifiable in 2D, so this sub-verdict is a consistency check, not a measurement of alpha
acceptance_criteria.c_gnomonic: |k_breadth - k_outer| / |k_outer| <= 0.25 along rays from the fitted pole (E4, projection-invariant); counted only where the ray test is conclusive (pole outside the structure, >= 60% valid rays, |r| >= 0.8 for both log-linear fits)
acceptance_criteria.verdict_rule: supported = a AND c on all testable sources AND b consistent; refuted = a fails on every Ovis source; otherwise mixed
acceptance_criteria.d_species_contrast: reported, not scored: Thompson predicts Capra alpha < Ovis alpha
